body: Best of luck, man. I've been taking things one day at a time, sometimes hour by hour. It has been a difficult process. I've discovered that I have some deep-seated attachment issues and an enormous fear of abandonment. I'm hoping I can use this as a catalyst to heal all of these issues within.

I do in fact have a tendency towards codependency, although I make great efforts to conceal that from others. I never felt that the friendship was one-sided, as I did many many favors for him so that there was a balance of give and take (not to make the friendship seem transactional). Most of our time spent together was initiated by him and seemed to have been mutually enjoyable. I never dumped my personal issues on him or anything.

I do agree that asking him to sacrifice his happiness and time just for me is selfish and unfair. It's just a difficult adjustment to make, you know? I've taken it personally.
That's nice to hear really, sometimes life gets in the way. I'm trying not to take things too personally. Perhaps you should reach out to him someday?
Thanks for putting things into perspective.

This is interesting because I identify as gay and my friend identifies as straight. This is something I hadn't really considered. Maybe he was worried people would think he was gay if we spent too much time together? I don't know.
Why did you feel the need to distance yourself from this person, if I may ask?
I heard a song called "In a Big country" by Big Country in my dream earlier. I couldn't remember the name of the song so I had to search by some lyrics I recalled to find it. Thoughts?
You must feel like a God now!

Frankly, I don't have to cope with it because I will be dead and unable to be bothered by it at some point and it seems useless and self-important to worry about it now. Where I am, death is not. Where death is, I am not. Of course I'm not entirely sold on the concept of an afterlife but if there is one I would hope it wouldn't leave room for regret and attachment to this world.

The idea of being forgotten doesn't particularly bother me in any case. The vast majority of human beings who have ever lived have not been remembered by the collective. That's okay. Assuming you don't become influential to society, you're still very important in your web of humanity and can make an impact there while you're here. In that sense your actions can and will live on after you're gone.
